newsitem.title: USA: Columbia University to host 4-party Korea talks.
newsitem.headline: Columbia University to host 4-party Korea talks.

text.p: The first four-party talks aimed at negotiating a formal end to the 1950-53 Korean War will take place next month at Columbia University's School of International and Public Affairs in New York, university sources said on Monday.

State Department officials declined to confirm the precise site of the preparatory talks, scheduled to take place Aug. 5 in New York, but said they expected to make an announcement as early as Tuesday.
North Korea accepted on June 30 a 14-month-old joint U.S. and South Korean proposal to hold talks, along with China, aimed at replacing the 1953 truce that ended the war with a formal peace.
At the same time, the North agreed to take part in the New York preparatory session, which was to decide the date, venue, agenda and procedures for the formal start of Four-Party peace talks.
A State Department official said working-level officials from the United States and the Koreas were meeting in New York on Monday to study logistical arrangements for the preparatory meeting.
A Columbia University spokeswoman declined to confirm the university would host the session, saying the State Department would make any such announcement.
